en.headline: Legionnaires’ disease linked to hospital water dispenser
en.dek: An 89-year-old patient at Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital is highly likely to have contracted the disease from a cooled-boiled-water device that tested positive for Legionella, the Centre for Health Protection said.
body: The Centre for Health Protection said an 89-year-old man hospitalised at Hong Kong Sanatorium & Hospital in Happy Valley is highly likely to have contracted Legionnaires’ disease after drinking water from a contaminated dispenser. Water samples from devices dispensing cooled boiled water tested positive for Legionella pneumophila at levels far above the action threshold for high-risk hospital areas.

Genetic testing showed the bacteria matched the strain found in the patient’s respiratory specimen. The hospital has stopped using the affected dispensers and is providing bottled water as a temporary measure. A total of 137 patients who stayed on the same floor are under medical surveillance; none has developed the disease so far.

The patient had been admitted since April for underlying illnesses. His shortness of breath worsened in early July and a respiratory sample later tested positive. His condition improved after antibiotic treatment. The Centre for Health Protection continues to follow up the case.

zh.headline: 養和醫院退伍軍人病個案與飲水機有關
zh.dek: 衞生防護中心表示，一名89歲男病人很大可能因飲用受污染的凍開水飲水機供水而感染退伍軍人病，同層137名病人已納入醫學監察。
body: 衞生防護中心表示，一名在跑馬地養和醫院留醫的89歲男病人，很大可能因飲用受污染的凍開水飲水機供水而感染退伍軍人病。醫院內提供凍開水的飲水機水樣本驗出嗜肺軍團菌，濃度遠超醫院高風險區域供水系統的行動水平。
基因檢測顯示，水樣本細菌與病人呼吸道樣本的菌株吻合。醫院已全面停用有關飲水機，並暫時改以樽裝水供應。同層137名住院病人已納入醫學監察，至今無人發病。
該病人自4月起因本身疾病住院，7月初氣促加劇，其後呼吸道樣本確診。經抗生素治療後情况改善。衞生防護中心繼續跟進事件。
